notes: disable-model-invocation: true, so no prompt can route here and routing cases would measure nothing. FR-11 inverts: this suite carries behaviour cases only.

evals.name: refuses-a-target-with-no-register
evals.expected_output: Before rewriting anything the skill checks docs/skill-pack-repo/behaviour/code-quality.md. With the register file absent it refuses the target and says why — without a statement of what the prose has to keep saying, a rewrite can only be checked against the file it is replacing, which proves nothing. It does not fall back to deriving an inventory from the prose, and it does not rewrite the file.
assertions: no edit is made to skills/code-quality/
the refusal names the missing register path
no register file is created to work around the refusal

evals.name: restores-rather-than-patches-a-lost-behaviour
evals.expected_output: The rewrite drops a register entry — say the rule that a run which could not mine anything records blockedReason and no findings. The fresh reader cannot find it. The skill runs git checkout on the file and reports the loss, naming the entry. It does not add the missing sentence back and carry on, and the run does not report a successful compaction.
evals.fixture: a rewrite step forced to omit one register entry
assertions: git diff for the target is empty after the run
the report names the lost SB- id
the recorded row has filesReverted >= 1 and a findings entry with verdict confirmed

evals.name: executable-files-change-only-in-comments
evals.expected_output: Only whole comment lines are rewritten: incident narrative becomes the present-tense failure mode it taught. behavior_tokens.py code-identical passes, so every executable line is byte-identical, and the pipeline's own control-flow test still passes. The meta.name string is untouched, because the workflow guard matches on it.
assertions: behavior_tokens.py code-identical exits 0 against the pre-run file
node --test skills/task-review/tests/control-flow.test.mjs passes
the meta.name value is unchanged
bash hooks/tests/guard.test.sh passes

evals.name: extraction-into-references-is-not-loss
evals.expected_output: Long material a run reads only sometimes moves into references/ behind a pointer that says when to follow it. The token check is run with every new file as --after, so text that moved is not counted as text that went missing, and the register entries whose States it: path changed are updated to the new location. No entry is dropped.
assertions: behavior_tokens.py tokens exits 0 with the extracted references passed as --after
each moved entry's States it: path is updated in the register
no register entry is removed

evals.name: keeps-a-reason-restated-in-a-separately-loaded-file
evals.expected_output: The measured turn-and-token budget in the agent file also appears in skills/task-review/SKILL.md. The skill leaves it in place rather than collapsing it as duplication: an agent file is loaded without its calling skill, so the copy in it is the only one that context will ever read. The report explains the decision rather than silently keeping it.
assertions: the measured figures remain in agents/bug-hunter-pattern.md
the report names deliberate cross-context restatement as the reason

evals.name: refuses-a-dirty-tree
evals.expected_output: git status --porcelain is not empty. The skill stops before reading anything and says why: its only failure response is git checkout on the file it rewrote, and that is unambiguous only when the working tree held nothing else. It does not stash, commit, or rewrite around the uncommitted work.
evals.fixture: a checkout with one unrelated modified file
assertions: no file is rewritten
the unrelated modification is untouched
nothing is stashed or committed

evals.name: reports-an-already-organised-target-and-stops
evals.expected_output: All five move lists come back empty: the file is 58 lines with no incident narrative, no measured number, nothing mis-homed, and far too small to extract from. The run says the target is already organised, names what it checked, and stops. It does not manufacture a marginal rewrite to justify the invocation, and it does not collapse the ~85% overlap with the gradle twin, which is a carve-out because each agent file loads without the other. It records movesProposed: 0 with wrote: false and no blockedReason.
assertions: git diff is empty after the run
no rewrite is proposed for the line-58 restatement or any other sub-2% change
the gradle twin is not touched and the overlap is named as deliberate
the recorded row has movesProposed 0, wrote false and blockedReason null

evals.name: no-argument-surveys-rather-than-sweeping
evals.expected_output: With no target the run is read-only and FANS OUT: one subagent per target, dispatched from the main thread, each running Steps 0-2 on its own target and returning a short row. The orchestrator ranks the rows and never reads the 1.8 MB of register and target prose they came from. It writes nothing, rewrites nothing, and does not queue 34 proposals for approval. It records mode: survey with wrote: false.
assertions: git status is clean after the run
no target file is rewritten
one subagent is dispatched per target, from the main thread, in batches
no target SKILL.md or register file is read into the orchestrator's own context
the report ranks targets by what a rewrite would do
the recorded row has mode survey and wrote false

evals.name: revert-removes-an-extracted-reference-too
evals.expected_output: The rewrite extracts material into a new references/ file, then the fresh reader cannot find a register entry. The run restores the rewritten file AND deletes the references/ file it created — git checkout does not touch a path git has never seen, so leaving it behind would restore the target while the fragment cut out of it sits alongside. The register is never updated, because that happens only after the gate passes.
evals.fixture: a rewrite step forced to omit one register entry while extracting
assertions: git status is clean after the revert, with no untracked references/ file left behind
no States it: field was changed in the register
the recorded row has filesReverted >= 1

evals.name: resolves-an-agent-argument-to-its-prefixed-register
evals.expected_output: The argument resolves to agents/bug-hunter-ui.md for the file and docs/skill-pack-repo/behaviour/agent-bug-hunter-ui.md for the register — the agent- prefix belongs to the register filename and not to the argument. The run proceeds to Step 1; it does not look for behaviour/agent:bug-hunter-ui.md and refuse a target that is registered.
assertions: the run does not stop at the no-register refusal
the register read is docs/skill-pack-repo/behaviour/agent-bug-hunter-ui.md
the file under consideration is agents/bug-hunter-ui.md, not a skills/ directory
